w:r.w:t: VIT FOOD SPOT GUIDE: AI-POWERED, LOCATION-BASED CAMPUS FOOD DISCOVERY WEB APPLICATION
School of Computer Science and Engineering (SCOPE)
School of Computer Science and Engineering (SCOPE)

Vellore Institute of Technology (VIT), Vellore, accommodates an extensive residential academic population exceeding 35,000 students, faculty members, and administrative staff across a sprawling 372-acre campus. Campus dining options comprise over 28 independent dining establishments, multi-cuisine food courts, specialized kiosks, and hostel mess facilities distributed across geographically segregated sectors. However, due to the decentralized spatial layout and absence of a unified campus food directory, students routinely encounter substantial difficulties in locating dining outlets, identifying menu items, determining accurate prices, verifying dietary classifications (Pure Vegetarian, Non-Vegetarian, Halal), and discovering food spots proximate to specific academic blocks such as PRP (Periyar Research Park), SJT (Silver Jubilee Tower), and residential hostel complexes.

To eliminate this informational friction and enhance daily campus life, this project presents the "VIT Food Spot Guide: An AI-Powered, Location-Based Campus Food Discovery Web Application". Built as an end-to-end full-stack web programming system, the application centralizes campus food discovery through an intuitive, accessible web interface. The system implements a robust multi-tier architecture powered by a high-performance Node.js and Express backend coupled to a normalized MySQL relational database engine. Over 340 individual menu items across all 28 food spots are indexed with strict relational integrity, foreign key constraints, price thresholds, and dietary taxonomies. A localized SQLite relational portability engine ensures seamless offline operation and local development parity, while Java JDBC demonstration components illustrate enterprise relational database connectivity.

The client interface features an academic-aligned design system utilizing Warm Ivory (#F8F6EE) and Forest Green (#315C45) palettes with full light and dark mode compliance. Core capabilities include omni-search dish and outlet querying, multi-attribute filtering (Zone, Budget, Dietary preference, Food Category), interactive modal menu inspection, specialized Men's and Ladies' hostel dining directories (including One Food World food court and Flora), academic block proximity discovery, verified student reviews with star ratings, and student bookmarking. Furthermore, the system integrates a domain-grounded AI Campus Food Assistant that processes natural-language student inquiries and synthesizes precise, hallucination-free dining recommendations directly grounded in verified database records.

Extensive empirical testing, including automated unit tests, browser integration suites, and responsive UI validation, confirms that the VIT Food Spot Guide achieves sub-50ms database search response times, 100% schema compliance, complete cross-device usability, and zero unauthorized data fabrication, delivering a dependable, student-centric food discovery portal for VIT Vellore.

Vellore Institute of Technology (VIT) in Vellore, Tamil Nadu, is one of India's premier higher education institutions, featuring an expansive 372-acre campus that houses over 35,000 undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral students alongside several thousand faculty and operational personnel. The campus operates as a self-contained academic township featuring distinct geographical and functional zones: the Academic Zone (housing major multi-story instructional complexes such as Periyar Research Park [PRP], Silver Jubilee Tower [SJT], Mahatma Gandhi Block [MGB], Technology Tower [TT], G.D. Naidu Block [GDN], and Sir M. Visvesvaraya Block [SMV]), the Men's Hostel residential sectors (Blocks A through T), and the Ladies' Hostel residential sectors (Blocks A through G).

Dining infrastructure on campus is distributed among more than 28 distinct commercial and institutional food service outlets. These range from centralized multi-counter food courts like One Food World (OFW) in the Men's Hostel area and Flora Food Court in the Ladies' Hostel area to specialized brand kiosks (Just Bake, Nescafe outlets, Lipton corners), academic block cafeterias (Food Street, PRP Snack Bar, SJT Basement Canteen), and independent health food bars. Each establishment operates with unique operating hours, distinct price schedules, specific culinary specializations (North Indian, South Indian, Continental, Chinese, Tandoori, Fast Food, Healthy Beverages), and specific dietary categorizations.
Figure 1.1: VIT Vellore Campus Topographical Map and Spatial Distribution of Dining Outlets
Despite the abundant culinary variety available on campus, students continually encounter severe friction in identifying, choosing, and accessing food due to several systemic challenges:

Food establishments are widely separated across a massive campus terrain. Walking from academic blocks such as PRP or SJT to residential dining zones requires 10 to 20 minutes, leading to wasted transit time when students are unaware of immediate nearby food options.

Dining outlets do not maintain digital or synchronized menus. Daily menu changes, fluctuating availability, and special seasonal offerings remain inaccessible until students physically visit the counter.

Students seeking specific culinary preparations (e.g., "Where can I get chicken biryani right now?", "Which outlet serves filter coffee near SJT?", "What wholesome lunch options exist under ₹100?") have no search mechanism and must rely on casual word-of-mouth.

VIT hosts a diverse domestic and international student body with strict dietary requirements, including Pure Vegetarian, Vegan, Eggetarian, and Non-Vegetarian. The lack of standardized dietary tags creates uncertainty and potential discomfort.
Students on student budgets lack transparent price comparison tools across outlets for staple items such as juices, meals, and snacks.
No centralized, verified peer-review platform exists for students to share genuine quality ratings, portion feedback, and hygiene observations.

The motivation behind developing the VIT Food Spot Guide is rooted in software engineering principles applied to real campus life. Modern web technologies, normalized relational database systems, and artificial intelligence provide the ideal foundation to bridge this information gap. By building a production-grade, responsive web application that unites location intelligence, relational menu indexing, community reviews, and database-grounded conversational AI, the project delivers an immediate, practical benefit to tens of thousands of VITians while demonstrating advanced full-stack web programming concepts.
The primary functional and academic objectives of this project are:
To design and implement a normalized relational database schema (MySQL) modeling campus locations, food spots, menu items, users, reviews, and student favorites with strict foreign key constraints.
To build an omni-search query engine capable of searching dishes and food spots concurrently with sub-50ms execution times.
To provide multi-dimensional filtering across Zone, Budget (Under ₹100, ₹100–₹200, ₹200+), Dietary tags (Veg, Non-Veg, Egg), and Category (Main Course, Snacks, Fast Food, Beverages, Desserts).
To architect location-aware discovery views for Men's Hostels, Ladies' Hostels, and key Academic Blocks (PRP — Periyar Research Park, SJT, MGB, TT, GDN, SMV).
To develop a database-grounded conversational AI assistant capable of parsing natural language campus food queries and generating factually accurate, hallucination-free advice.
To implement secure student authentication enforcing official VIT student email formats (@vitstudent.ac.in) and Bcrypt password hashing.
To engineer a polished, academic UI design system featuring Warm Ivory and Forest Green palettes with verified contrast compliance across Light and Dark themes.

The project scope encompasses all commercial and institutional food service outlets physically located inside the VIT Vellore main campus. It includes 28 verified food spots and 340+ cataloged menu items. The system provides self-service exploration, menu inspection, location guidance, peer feedback submission, and conversational recommendations. External commercial off-campus delivery logistics and online financial transactions (payment gateways) are intentionally kept outside the operational scope to preserve focus on core campus food discovery, relational database performance, and web application integrity.
The VIT Food Spot Guide is structured into seven tightly integrated functional modules designed to deliver a cohesive, frictionless user experience:

The Explore module serves as the primary gateway and central discovery hub of the web application. It features an interactive omni-search input capable of processing freeform text queries for dishes (e.g., "Biryani", "Dosa", "Sandwich", "Coffee") or outlet names. Complementing search is a multi-dimensional filter bar supporting compound criteria: Location / Zone dropdown, Dietary preference selector (All, Pure Veg, Non-Veg, Egg), Budget range selector (Under ₹100, ₹100–₹200, ₹200+), and Food Category selector (Main Course, Fast Food, Snacks, Beverages, Desserts).

Matching food spots are rendered in an ergonomic responsive grid. Each outlet card exhibits high-level visual metadata: establishment name, geographic zone tag, operational status badge (Open / Closed), cuisine tags, average star rating, review count, price tier, and an interactive bookmark toggle. Clicking any card activates the Food Spot Detail Modal, which queries the backend for the complete categorized menu, displaying dish descriptions, prices, and dietary indicator badges.

The Men's Hostel module focuses on dining infrastructure surrounding the Men's residential blocks (Blocks A through T). Central to this module is One Food World (OFW), the largest centralized food court in the men's residential sector. The module breaks down OFW into its specialized constituent food counters:
Serving parathas, butter chicken, dal makhani, paneer gravies, and tandoori rotis.
Specializing in dosas, idlis, vadas, meals, and uttapams.
Offering fried rice, noodles, manchurian, and momos.
Serving freshly baked pastries, patties, rolls, and cakes.
Providing hot beverages, cold coffee, iced tea, and instant snacks.
Dedicated to the residential students of Ladies' Hostels (Blocks A through G), this module highlights safe, proximate, and nutritious dining establishments:
The primary food court offering hygienic vegetarian and non-vegetarian daily meals, chaats, and multi-cuisine dinners.
Renowned for comforting home-style South Indian tiffins, dosas, and meals at economical prices.
Quick refreshment and coffee hub situated within the hostel perimeter.
Fresh seasonal fruit juices, milkshakes, fruit bowls, and wholesome vegetable salads.

During rigorous instructional schedules, students require quick, accessible sustenance between lectures and laboratory sessions without commuting back to hostel zones. The Academic Blocks module provides targeted proximity discovery for:
Houses the popular Food Street cafeteria, Juice & Snack Bar, and quick-bite counters serving fresh biryani, rolls, and cold drinks.
Features the high-traffic SJT Basement Cafeteria and Ground Floor Kiosk, ideal for quick breakfast and evening refreshments.
Technology Tower food court and bakery counter.

The AI Campus Food Assistant represents an intelligent conversational layer bridging natural human questions and structured relational campus data. Rather than relying on unconstrained large language model generations that hallucinate non-existent campus restaurants, the assistant employs a strict Database Grounding Architecture. When a user asks questions such as "Where can I get biryani near PRP?" or "What can I eat under ₹100?", the system queries the relational database, extracts verified matching records, and synthesizes structured, natural language responses detailing exact outlet names, prices, and locations.

The Feedback module democratizes campus dining by providing an authentic student rating platform. Authenticated students can submit 1 to 5 star ratings, specify particular dishes reviewed, and author qualitative commentary. The community review feed displays ratings, timestamps, and helpfulness upvotes, establishing peer-verified quality transparency.

Students can bookmark favorite outlets and specific dishes by clicking the heart icon across any card or menu item. The Favorites view aggregates saved spots, enabling instantaneous one-click menu access and personalized shortcuts.

The non-functional characteristics governing system quality include:
Relational SQL search queries must execute in under 50 milliseconds. Initial page payload delivery must complete in under 1.2 seconds on standard campus Wi-Fi.
The interface adheres to intuitive web heuristics, featuring zero dead clicks, prominent feedback alerts, and clear visual card affordances.

All student passwords are irreversibly hashed using the Bcrypt algorithm with salt factor 10. Database interactions utilize parameterized SQL queries to eliminate SQL injection vulnerabilities. Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) is mitigated via DOM text escaping.

The backend incorporates an automatic SQLite relational fallback engine. If the production MySQL service is unreachable, the system transparently initializes the local SQLite database without interrupting client operations.
The UI system is engineered with responsive CSS Grid and Flexbox mechanics, ensuring visual fidelity across mobile smartphones (320px+), tablets (768px+), and desktop workstations (1280px+).

The VIT Food Spot Guide adopts a classical Multi-Tier Client-Server Architecture engineered for high concurrency, clear separation of concerns, and data integrity:

Executed within the client browser. Features responsive HTML5 semantics, CSS3 Custom Properties, and modular JavaScript/jQuery orchestration. All communication with the server is conducted asynchronously via RESTful JSON APIs.
Powered by Node.js and Express. Handles route dispatching, request authentication, rate limiting, data validation, and controller business logic.
Composed of normalized MySQL relational database tables enforcing foreign key constraints and indexed queries. A transparent SQLite relational fallback provides portability.

4.1.4 Relational Database Design and Data Dictionary
The relational database is normalized to Third Normal Form (3NF) to eliminate data redundancy and preserve referential integrity. The schema is organized into six interconnected relational tables:
Unique surrogate identifier for campus location
Full descriptive name (e.g., Periyar Research Park)
Standard campus acronym (e.g., PRP, SJT, MH, LH)
Topographical location notes and landmark landmarks
Unique identifier for food spot outlet
Official name (e.g., Sri Sai Sabari, One Food World)
Primary cuisine type (e.g., North Indian, South Indian)
Foreign key referencing owning food establishment
Dish name (e.g., Chicken Biryani, Paneer Butter Masala)
Detailed culinary description, ingredients, or portions
Dietary tag: Pure Veg, Non-Veg, Egg
Student popular pick flag (1 = True, 0 = False)
Current inventory status (1 = Available, 0 = Out of stock)
Unique identifier for student user account
Foreign key referencing reviewed food spot
Identifier of saved food spot or menu item
4.1.5 User Interface Design and Visual System

The visual system for the VIT Food Spot Guide was engineered to reflect academic restraint, readability, and modern elegance. Rather than utilizing generic corporate blueprints or distracting saturated neon gradients, the interface establishes a distinctive, campus-appropriate identity founded on Warm Ivory and Forest Green tones:

Primary light mode background, canvas warmth, modal headers
Primary brand anchor, header text, navigation pills, primary CTAs
Dark theme background surface, card borders, high-contrast headings
Secondary buttons, hover states, badge outlines, icon accents
Pill backgrounds, search box shading, subtle card separators
Star rating displays, bookmark highlights, premium badges

Theme switching is executed cleanly via CSS Custom Properties toggled on the root document element (document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark")). In dark mode, card surfaces transform into deep slate hues (--bg-card: #223028), input fields adapt without contrast wash, and text variables elevate to crisp off-white tones, preserving complete WCAG 2.1 AA readability.
The frontend search and filtering orchestrator in client/js/app.js handles real-time user inputs, coordinates asynchronous API requests, and executes client-side state updates:

if (diet && diet !== 'all' && d.dietary !== diet) return false;
if (cat && cat !== 'all' && d.category !== cat) return false;

const { q, dietary, maxPrice, category, zone } = req.query;
